artifacts.summary: Measured deploy-drift state (44 commits / 16 files since deploy, 11 gate5 findings across 8 script-level + 3 doc-level items), confirmed all three description premises, identified the four completed tasks that become live at this deploy (mint-dispatch-seq fix, three literature fixes incl. HIGH-severity corpus-corruption gate), captured a verbatim PRE-deploy verify-deploy.sh --findings baseline, assessed both deferred decisions as DEFER with reasons, and found deploy risk low since only agent-system/ changes matter and all trace to completed tasks.

memory_candidates.content: verify-deploy.sh --findings --quiet is the authoritative pre/post deploy drift baseline; its gate5 'deployed vs source' check does NOT cover manifest.json files or all context-pattern docs, so a clean gate5 pass does not prove those files deployed correctly -- confirm with a direct diff -q by hand for manifest.json and pattern docs specifically.

When measuring 'commits/files since last deploy', use the batch mtime cluster of deployed .claude/ files (find .claude -type f -printf '%T@ %p\n' | sort -rn, excluding tmp/) as the true deploy timestamp, not a rounded '7 days ago'. Individually-resynced files (e.g. via picker Ctrl-l) carry a distinct newer mtime and are byte-identical to source -- exclude them from the drift set even though git shows them as recently changed.

deploy-headless.sh deploys only from agent-system/extensions/** (the source store), never from specs/ (task-management). When assessing deploy risk from 'N commits since last deploy', filter to commits touching agent-system/ only -- repo-wide commit counts vastly overstate deploy-relevant risk since specs/ churn (TODO.md, state.json, task dirs) dominates commit volume but is deploy-irrelevant.
